lines.text: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and answer me,
for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my soul, for I am godly.
You are my God; save Your servant who trusts in You.
Be merciful to me, O Lord,
for I call to You all day long.
for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
For You, O Lord, are kind and forgiving,
rich in loving devotion to all who call on You.
and attend to my plea for mercy.
In the day of my distress I call on You,

pictures.scene: Eastman Johnson, The Lord Is My Shepherd — the old man bent over the open book in the lamplight, a prayer of David, incline Your ear O LORD and answer me
pictures.name: pd_johnson_shepherd

pictures.scene: David Adolph Constant Artz, Bij grootmoeder — the bare cottage room with the child at the old woman's knee, for I am poor and needy, preserve my soul for I am godly
pictures.name: pd_artz_grootmoeder

pictures.scene: Esaias van de Velde, A landscape with Christ and the Canaanite woman — the woman kneeling in the road to beg of Him, You are my God save Your servant who trusts in You, be merciful to me O Lord
pictures.name: pd_velde_cananese

pictures.scene: Julien Dupré, Retour de troupeau — the herd driven home across the field at the end of the day, for I call to You all day long, bring joy to Your servant
pictures.name: pd_dupre_troupeau

pictures.scene: Eugène Jansson, Sunrise over the Rooftops — the first light coming up over the sleeping town, for to You O Lord I lift up my soul, for You O Lord are kind and forgiving
pictures.name: pd_jansson_soluppgang

pictures.scene: Pierre Mignard, Christ and the Woman of Samaria — the stranger at the well given more than she came for, rich in loving devotion to all who call on You, hear my prayer O LORD
pictures.name: pd_mignard_samaritaanse

pictures.scene: Pieter Aertsen, De genezing van de lamme van Bethesda — the helpless man lifted up from his mat at the pool, and attend to my plea for mercy, in the day of my distress I call on You
pictures.name: pd_aertsen_bethesda

pictures.scene: Jacob Pynas, Paulus en Barnabas te Lystra door het volk als goden vereerd — the crowd bringing garlands to men who refuse them, because You answer me, O Lord there is none like You among the gods
pictures.name: pd_pynas_lystra
